svg.title: Where the code is, by pipeline stage
svg.desc: Lines of C++ per stage. Inside the scheduler package almost everything is task planning; the motion planner's size is in the motion_planner package, most of which the scheduler uses; the action graph is small.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: solid: scheduler package pale, dashed outline: library package

g.text: Scheduler: function definitions in scheduler.cpp and utils.cpp, grouped by the stage that calls them (4,574 of 4,721 lines; the rest is includes and namespaces). Libraries: every .hpp and .cpp in the motion_planner, planner_core and cost_functions snapshots; 'never called'

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: = no call path from the scheduler's code (found by tracing calls from its sources). Not counted: task_planner (BottleneckAssignment, not in the snapshots), common_ros (the garage model, about 9,800 lines, used by every stage) and tests (6,546 lines in scheduler, mostly

g.text: Lines of C++ (headers and sources, without tests). In the scheduler package, task planning is about 3,590 of 4,570 lines (78%), the motion-planning adapter 63, the action graph about 540. Counting the library code the scheduler

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: actually calls, task planning is about 5,000 lines and motion planning about 3,900; about 660 lines of motion_planner are never called. The action graph stays small.
